nfl.oneThing: The 49ers beat the Cowboys 46–40 in a shootout at AT&T Stadium, with Brock Purdy throwing for 389 yards and Christian McCaffrey catching two touchdowns. Dallas allowed 584 yards, the third-most in the franchise's history.

headlines.title: 49ers outlast Cowboys in a 46–40 shootout
headlines.summary: Brock Purdy completed 22 of 28 passes for 389 yards and three touchdowns. McCaffrey added 161 receiving yards and two scores, and Deebo Samuel scored on the ground. Dak Prescott and George Pickens kept Dallas in it, with Prescott throwing five touchdowns and Pickens catching three. The 584 yards are the third-most the Cowboys have allowed in their history.
headlines.whyItMatters: San Francisco stays at the top of the NFC at 8–1. Dallas is 2.0 games behind the last playoff spot in the NFC, so the loss hurts its position.

headlines.title: Mahomes has his best game of the year in Chiefs' 35–13 win
headlines.summary: Patrick Mahomes threw for a season-high 348 yards and five touchdowns as Kansas City beat Atlanta 35–13. He played with a small sprain in his right UCL, suffered seven days earlier, and wore an elbow sleeve between drives. Kenneth Walker III missed his first game of the season with a groin injury, and Emmett Johnson ran for 101 yards in his place. Mahomes said he'd be icing the elbow on the flight home.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Chiefs move to 7–2 and stay second in the AFC. They have now shown they can win without their starting running back, which matters with injuries piling up.

headlines.title: Geno Smith hurt as Jets slump to fifth straight loss
headlines.summary: Geno Smith hurt his left ankle in the third quarter of the Jets' 31–12 loss to Buffalo and left on a golf cart. Coach Aaron Glenn has not given an update, and his status for Week 11 will be decided during the practice week. Rookie Cade Klubnik made his NFL debut, throwing an interception and being sacked three times. The Jets (2–8) have not scored a touchdown in nine quarters, their longest drought since 2023, and they are the second team this century to lose back-to-back games by at least 17 points despite having four scoring drives in each.
headlines.whyItMatters: Their quarterback situation is now unclear with the offence already struggling badly.

headlines.title: Rams roll past Cardinals for fourth straight win
headlines.summary: Los Angeles beat Arizona 34–6 on Sunday, overcoming a slow start. Matthew Stafford threw for 249 yards and three touchdowns, and Blake Corum ran for 100 yards and a touchdown. Sean McVay used Corum and Kyren Williams together while his top receivers were out. The Rams head into a Week 11 bye at 6–4.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Rams are 6–4 and in the NFC wild-card mix. The bye gives them time to rest and reset during the tight race.

headlines.title: Seahawks, Packers and Rams bunched at the NFC's last playoff spots
headlines.summary: Seattle won, and Green Bay also won, so the Seahawks are tied with the Packers for the seventh and final NFC playoff spot. Green Bay holds that spot on the wild-card tiebreaker, and Seattle is eighth. The Rams are ninth. The Seahawks have won three of their last four and are at 6–4, the same record as Green Bay and Los Angeles.
headlines.whyItMatters: The NFC wild-card race is very tight. Three teams at 6–4 are fighting for one spot, and tiebreakers are deciding the order.

teamNews.title: Brock Bowers out with ankle injury
teamNews.text: Bowers was ruled out of the 21–13 loss to Seattle after hurting his right ankle in the opening quarter. He was listed as questionable before being ruled out, and coach Klint Kubiak said he would be reevaluated on Monday.

teamNews.title: Mendoza's first start ends in a 21–13 loss
teamNews.text: Fernando Mendoza started his first NFL game and ran for a touchdown. He was sacked six times, finishing with 17 completions in 29 attempts for 143 yards and no passing touchdowns. Seattle outscored Las Vegas after halftime, with the Raiders managing negative yards until their last possession.

teamNews.title: Three Raiders inactive, Runyon promoted
teamNews.text: Malik Benson, Dont'e Thornton Jr. and Thomas Booker IV were inactive against Seattle. Tight end Carter Runyon was elevated from the practice squad.

teamNews.title: Cousins makes Vikings debut in win over Packers
teamNews.text: Kirk Cousins threw two touchdown passes in his first game after the Raiders traded him to Minnesota. The Vikings beat Green Bay 30–10, and Cousins was emotional afterwards about his return.

recaps.keyLine: Lock 14/17, 240 yds, 2 TD · Smith-Njigba 8 rec, 171 yds, 1 TD · Mendoza 17/29, 143 yds, 0 TD · Crosby 1 sack, 8 tkl
recaps.text: The Raiders led 10–7 at halftime after Mendoza opened with a rushing touchdown and a quick scoring drive. Seattle then took over. Drew Lock threw two scramble-drill touchdowns, and Las Vegas had negative yards until its final drive. Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 71-yard touchdown from Lock was the game-breaker. For the Raiders, the question now is whether Mendoza can handle the pressure after a start that promised more.

recaps.keyLine: Purdy 22/28, 389 yds, 3 TD · McCaffrey 4 rec, 161 yds, 2 TD · Prescott 30/51, 343 yds, 5 TD, 1 INT · Pickens 11 rec, 145 yds, 3 TD
recaps.text: Prescott's five touchdowns and Pickens's three were not enough to counter Purdy's accuracy and San Francisco's big plays. The Cowboys' defence gave up 584 yards, which is the kind of number that will get attention when Dallas is looking at its playoff chances.

recaps.keyLine: Stroud 20/38, 211 yds, 3 TD, 1 INT · Collins 9 rec, 94 yds, 1 TD · Watson 25/40, 312 yds, 0 TD, 1 INT · Fannin Jr. 7 rec, 91 yds
recaps.text: Deshaun Watson led Cleveland to a 27–24 win over his former team, Houston, with a late drive. It was his sixth game-winning drive of the season, and he called it "definitely special". Watson threw for 312 yards, but also had an interception, and the defence closed out the game. The Browns move to 6–4 and are in the AFC playoff picture.

recaps.keyLine: Cousins 21/31, 207 yds, 2 TD, 1 INT · Jefferson 9 rec, 74 yds · Love 17/27, 220 yds, 1 TD, 1 INT · Golden 5 rec, 70 yds
recaps.text: Jordan Love threw for 220 yards but was under constant pressure from the Vikings' pass rush and was intercepted once. Cousins threw two touchdowns in his return.

recaps.keyLine: Lawrence 25/35, 352 yds, 3 TD, 1 INT · Washington 7 rec, 152 yds, 1 TD · Ward 28/39, 231 yds, 2 TD, 1 INT · Ayomanor 5 rec, 79 yds
recaps.text: Trevor Lawrence threw for 352 yards and three touchdowns as Jacksonville pulled away from Tennessee. Parker Washington's 152 receiving yards were the key target production, while Bhayshul Tuten ran for a touchdown. Tennessee's offence, led by Cam Ward, kept the score respectable, but the Titans remain at 1–8 with a long season ahead.

recaps.keyLine: McCord 17/32, 209 yds, 0 TD · Johnson 1 INT, 4 tkl, 1 TD · Jones 11/22, 108 yds, 1 TD, 2 INT · Allen 1 sack, 9 tkl
recaps.text: Indianapolis beat Miami 24–22 in a close finish, but the Colts' quarterback situation remains uncertain. Daniel Jones threw two interceptions and posted a 1.7 QBR, the lowest in the league this season. Coach Shane Steichen said Jones will remain the starter, citing the short week. Jonathan Taylor ran for 83 yards, which helped the Colts hang on.

recaps.keyLine: Young 17/30, 200 yds, 0 TD · Hubbard 27 car, 92 yds, 2 TD · Shough 25/35, 187 yds, 1 TD, 1 INT · Tyson 11 rec, 80 yds
recaps.text: Carolina beat New Orleans 20–17, with Chuba Hubbard the difference. He ran for 92 yards and two touchdowns, and caught five passes for 80 yards. Bryce Young struggled, with no touchdowns, but the defence held the Saints to 17 points. The Panthers move to 4–5, which keeps them in the NFC playoff mix.

contextCard.title: How NFL playoff seeding works
contextCard.body: Each conference has seven playoff teams. The four division winners take the top four seeds, ranked by record, and the other three teams are wild cards. The seeds decide who hosts each playoff game. When teams finish with the same record, tiebreakers decide the order, so a close race can come down to a division record or a head-to-head result.

nba.oneThing: The Spurs beat the Jazz 110–102 for their 12th straight win, and Dylan Harper's 31 points rallied them from behind. San Antonio is 12–2, the best record in the West, and Utah is on a 12-game losing streak.

headlines.title: Dončić scores 43 as Lakers hold off Suns for eighth straight win
headlines.summary: Luka Dončić scored 43 points, his seventh game of 40 or more in 12 games this season, as the Lakers beat Phoenix 131–123. He leads the league in scoring at 38.6 points a game. The Lakers led 101–70 with under two minutes left in the third quarter, then saw the Suns cut the margin to five late in the fourth. Quentin Grimes hit a bank-in three with 32.2 seconds left to seal it.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Lakers are 12–2 and level with San Antonio for the NBA's best record. Their eight-game win streak is building their position in the West.

headlines.title: Celtics open up a 42–9 lead over the Mavericks
headlines.summary: Boston led Dallas 42–9 after one quarter, the largest lead at the end of a quarter in franchise history. It was the best scoring margin by any team in a quarter since 1987, and tied for the third-best in the shot clock era. The Celtics shot 59% and made seven threes, while the Mavericks went 0-for-8 from three. Boston led 67–37 at halftime, and the Celtics have now led by 40 or more in three games this season.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Celtics are 10–2 and top of the East. Dallas, at 7–6, dropped one of its games after a loss in Cleveland the night before.

headlines.title: Clippers beat Hornets for 17th straight time
headlines.summary: Darius Garland scored 27 points, and the Clippers beat Charlotte 113–105, overcoming a 13-point deficit in the third quarter. Max Strus scored 14 off the bench. Charlotte coach Charles Lee was ejected after two technical fouls in a 17-second stretch. The Clippers have won three of their last four after a 1–7 start, and Brandon Ingram is still waiting for his season debut.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Clippers are 4–8 and their turnaround is picking up pace. The Hornets have lost eight of nine and open a four-game road trip at 0–2.

headlines.title: Bulls upset Timberwolves 117–106
headlines.summary: Chicago beat Minnesota 117–106. Norman Powell scored 24 points, and Matas Buzelis had 18 points and nine rebounds. LaMelo Ball had 19 points, eight rebounds and six assists for Minnesota. The Wolves then lost Jaylen Clark for at least two weeks with a right hamstring strain, which leaves them shorthanded on the wing.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Wolves have to cover for Clark while he is out.

headlines.title: LeBron passes Jason Kidd for third on the all-time assists list
headlines.summary: LeBron James had 11 assists in the 76ers' 131–124 win over Indiana, which moved him past Jason Kidd for third on the career assists list with 12,092. Jaylen Brown had a season-high score, and Tyrese Maxey also contributed as Philadelphia played without Joel Embiid. Tacko Fall got his first real minutes at centre.
headlines.whyItMatters: Philadelphia moves to 11–3 and sits second in the East. James' record is a milestone that will get attention all season.

recaps.text: The Spurs trailed for much of the fourth quarter before Dylan Harper's back-to-back threes tied it at 100. Stephon Castle's steal and dunk then pushed the lead to six, and Keldon Johnson's putback sealed a late run. Utah's 19–7 run in the third and fourth quarters had cut into a nine-point lead, but San Antonio held on. The win keeps the Spurs top of the West and extends their streak to 12.

Charlotte outrebounded them 46–37 and took 18 more shots, but the Clippers made their chances count. Coach Charles Lee's ejection in the third quarter added to Charlotte's problems. The Clippers have now beaten the Hornets 17 straight times.

The Lakers pushed it to 31 in the third, but Phoenix came back late and made it close. Quentin Grimes's bank-in three in the closing seconds was the play that ended the Suns' comeback.

recaps.text: Chicago beat the Timberwolves with a steady performance from Norman Powell and Matas Buzelis. Minnesota had LaMelo Ball and Ayo Dosunmu on the floor, but their offence could not keep pace. The upset is a reminder that the Bulls are not as weak as their record suggests, and Minnesota now has to adjust without Clark.

Tyrese Proctor had 24 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists for the Cavaliers, and Mario Hezonja added 22 points. The Mavericks were without their usual balance on the night, and Irving's scoring was not enough to keep them close.
